rationale: B wins because it keeps the best three pitches inside the evidence and makes the proof gates explicit. Its line, "Allbirds says its new sugarcane-and-wool shoe outlasts the original wool runner — now it has to prove it," has the right posture: sharp, skeptical, and grounded. A has better newsroom packaging, but "Allbirds Quietly Dropped 'Eco-Friendly' as Its Main Pitch" and "For a Brand Built on Cutting Out Middlemen" assert strategic history the update did not give. That is how a decent pitch turns into a correction waiting to happen.
gaps_in_A: "Allbirds Quietly Dropped 'Eco-Friendly' as Its Main Pitch" is an invented positioning shift. The update says durability is claimed; it does not say eco messaging was dropped.
"For a Brand Built on Cutting Out Middlemen" imports an anti-wholesale D2C origin story that is not in the supplied facts.
"wreckage of the 2021 D2C IPO cohort" and "went public too early" add outside context the prompt did not provide. Useful if verified, dirty if not.
The next step says the durability angle is "ready to draft once the partner name is confirmed," but that angle needs durability evidence, not the wholesale partner name.
gaps_in_B: "store closures plus a 40% product-range cut producing the first quarter of gross-margin improvement" implies causation the update does not prove.
"Allbirds' comeback runs through someone else's shelves" is a little too triumphant for an unprofitable company with one named wholesale partnership.
"category-creation" is the wrong label. This is a product-claim verification angle, not a category-creation story.
It leaves the public-market tension underused; "trades well below its IPO price" is strong investor context and deserved more than background placement.
